Thanks Linh — sorry for the friction.

Short note on root cause we see: during the last EU/US DST switchover window, some Calendly embed widgets fallback to the browser locale for display while leaving the event timezone anchored to the host. That mismatch shows a wrong hour when attendees accept the invite in certain calendar apps. Chili Piper has had a similar quirk where the auto-detect prefers the browser locale too. 

Workarounds I recommend (we've used all three with customers):
1) Manual timezone selector in Calendly (top-right) — choose Asia/Tokyo.
2) Use the alternate Chili Piper redirect (https://app.chilipiper.com/redirect?token=abc123) which forces the attendee to confirm timezone before booking.
3) I'll send a dedicated .ics (attached) set explicitly to JST with the Zoom URL; please accept that invite — that will place the event correctly in Outlook/Google Calendar.

Attaching: redwood-demo-proposed-times.ics (JST primary) and a small text file with direct Zoom link so mobile recipients can join without relying on calendar apps: redwood-demo-zoom-link.txt

If that still fails for anyone, we can also send a plain-text calendar event in the body with the meeting URL and ask recipients to manually add. Not ideal but works.

I'll send the JST invite now for Tue Mar 30 10:00–10:30 JST.

— Sergio
